``width``/``height`` are in ``units`` (``"in"`` or ``"px"``); ``dpi``
converts between the two and sets raster resolution. ``theme`` overrides
the spec's theme name. ``adapter`` pins a renderer by name; otherwise one
is selected by capability.

ieeVisualizer.render.base.RenderWarning.doc:
A fidelity warning attached to a render.

``code`` is a stable identifier, ``message`` a sentence naming what was
lost or approximated, ``path`` a JSON pointer into the spec ("" when the
warning is about the request or the figure as a whole).

ieeVisualizer.spec._common.ValidationIss.doc:
One structured finding about a spec.

``path`` is an RFC-6901 JSON pointer into the *serialized* spec (the same
pointer an agent would pass to :func:`apply_patch` to fix it), ``code`` is
a stable machine-readable identifier, ``message`` is a readable sentence
that names the fix, and ``severity`` is ``"error"``, ``"warning"`` or
``"info"``. Only errors make a spec unrenderable.

A complete, renderer-independent figure description.

``datasets`` maps a name to a :class:`DataSnapshot` or :class:`DatasetRef`;
each layer's ``data`` refers to one of those names. ``axes`` is keyed by

The column *name* is not fixed: ``parameter`` names the template parameter
whose value is the column name (or list of names, for ``column_list``
parameters). ``dtypes`` lists the accepted spec dtypes. ``unit``:
``"recommended"`` (a missing unit is reported as a warning unless the
template has another source for it) or ``"not_applicable"``.

``type`` is a key of :data:`PARAM_TYPES`. ``default`` is used when the
caller omits the parameter (``None`` means "unset"); a parameter with
``required=True`` has no default. ``allowed`` restricts the value to a
fixed set.
